name: Cache-Optimized Context Engineering
executive_summary: Structural layout optimized for API-level prefix caching (e.g., Anthropic Prompt Caching, OpenAI Prompt Caching). Places static content first to maximize cache hits, reducing latency and token cost substantially, per the providers' own published figures.
description: Modern LLM APIs offer prefix caching: if the initial portion of a prompt (the prefix) is identical across requests, the provider caches the KV activations and only charges for the new suffix tokens. Cache-Optimized Context Engineering explicitly structures prompts with a long static prefix followed by a short dynamic suffix.
when_to_use: High-volume APIs where the same system instructions and tool schemas are reused across thousands of requests.
When using providers that support prefix caching.
RAG systems where retrieved documents vary but the retrieval prompt structure is fixed.
when_not_to_use: Providers that do not support prefix caching.
Applications where every prompt is unique with no reusable prefix.
When the static prefix is shorter than the provider's minimum cache window.
known_pitfalls: Cache hit rate depends on exact byte-level prefix matching.
Provider cache TTL may be short; monitor cache hit metrics.
Over-optimizing for cache may hurt readability or maintainability.

primary_source.title: Prompt Engineering Best Practices: Prefix Caching

usage_templates.template:
<!-- STATIC PREFIX (Prefix-Cached across requests) -->
[SYSTEM INSTRUCTIONS / PERSONA]
{{system_instructions}}

[TOOL SCHEMAS / API DEFINITIONS]
{{tool_schemas}}

[FEW-SHOT EXEMPLAR BLOCK]
{{few_shot_exemplars}}

<!-- DYNAMIC SUFFIX (Appended per request) -->
[RETRIEVED CONTEXT / DOCUMENT PASSAGES]
{{retrieved_context}}

[USER QUERY]
{{user_query}}

variables.name: system_instructions
variables.description: Static system prompt reused across all requests.
variables.example: You are a helpful medical assistant. Be concise and evidence-based.

variables.name: tool_schemas
variables.description: Static tool/API definitions reused across requests.

variables.name: few_shot_exemplars
variables.description: Static few-shot examples reused across requests.
variables.example: Q: What is hypertension? A: Hypertension is high blood pressure...

variables.name: retrieved_context
variables.description: Dynamic retrieved documents unique to each request.
variables.example: Document 1: Recent study on ACE inhibitors...

variables.name: user_query
variables.example: What are the side effects of lisinopril?

usage_templates.reproducibility_note: The static prefix must be byte-identical across requests to trigger cache hits. Any change (whitespace, ordering, content) invalidates the cache.
